All six roots include project-only learner records/observations. Operator ID selection preserves current scope and retirement; ordinary body routes retain denial checks.

Plans bind actual affected row versions and matching retention facts, current scope/policy, database instance/file/revision and denial generations. New facts without content revision still invalidate plans. Overflow never issues a partial fingerprint.

Purge and immutable intent commit atomically. Historical retries never repurge newly restored content; canonical cleanup is separately pending/complete and never asserts current body absence or full sync.

Both council rounds returned Meta/Qwen/Mistral. Receipt, scope and body-route concerns were checked against code and directed tests; no unanimous approval claimed. Full selector diff was not in the council packet.

Removed peer config does not prevent local discard. Re-adding config alone cannot restore content; fresh permitted transfer remains necessary. No extraction/adoption or independence claim is introduced.

Stage38 connects actual configured session-sync commands to strict forced-command SSH. Dedicated identity/known hosts, receiver-owned peer and fixed operations exclude wire-supplied SQL/paths; owner SSH setup is unchanged.

Both directions recover lost acceptance/receipt metadata before reconciling permission/retirement controls. Content waits for stable control state; eight changing rounds refuse rather than promise convergence.

Broad tests exposed seeded-counter collision and invalid archival counter comparison. New-instance compaction keeps local counters; archival proof still compares actual rows. Overflow rolls back the triggering body write; excluded work invalidates shortcut without export.
